credit: NASA Earth Observatory — Blue Marble Next Generation (Reto Stöckli); elevation image derived from GEBCO

headers.height-encoding: uint8; RELATIVE only — no documented metre scale, and ocean floor is flat

note:
TWO LIMITATIONS, both the source's and both worth knowing before you use the height map.

1. It is 8-BIT, not 16. NASA publishes this global elevation image at 8 bits with no documented metre mapping, so it ships as it arrived. Promoting it to 16 bits would add bytes and no information and imply a precision it does not have; inventing a metre scale would be worse. Treat it as a relative bump map.
2. There is NO BATHYMETRY. Every ocean pixel is 0 — verified by sampling the mid-Pacific, the Mariana Trench and the mid-Atlantic. Land varies as expected (Sahara 21, Himalaya 125, Andes 143), so it is land elevation only, and a displaced sphere will have a billiard-ball sea floor.

If either matters, the fix is a real DEM — ETOPO 2022 is 16-bit and includes bathymetry — but it is NOAA rather than NASA, so it would want its own namespace.

Colour is the December 2004 Blue Marble topography+bathymetry composite, which DOES shade the ocean floor; it is only the elevation channel that is land-only.
